description: incrementAndCheck reads entry.count at line 86 and writes entry.count at line 96, but awaits persistAuditEvent at line 94 between the two — yielding the event loop. Two concurrent requests for the same IP both read count < MAX_REQUESTS, both pass the guard, and both increment, allowing up to 2× MAX_REQUESTS through before the limit engages.
persistAuditEvent silently swallows any rejection from the async write. If the audit store is unavailable the error is lost; callers get no signal and audit records are dropped without notification.

Changing incrementAndCheck from a synchronous boolean-returning function to an async Promise<boolean>-returning function is a breaking API change — all existing callers must now await the result or they compare a truthy Promise object instead of the boolean, silently bypassing the rate limit.
